From: Noah Patel <noah.patel@helixmedtech.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private Gateway: IP binding & egress policy questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for walking us through the private deployment options last week. Our security team is finalizing the firewall policy for the pilot VPC and asked for a few clarifications before we open the ticket to NetOps: 

1) Do you provide a small set of stable egress IPs we can allowlist, or do you require a NAT/proxy on our side?
2) If Redwood publishes egress IPs, will those be single IPs per region or a CIDR set? How often do they rotate?
3) What TLS/SNI behavior should we expect from the control-plane endpoints? Do you support mutual TLS for control plane?
4) Any outbound port ranges besides 443 to be aware of (metrics, health checks, RTP, etc.)?

We have a diagram attached that shows our transit NATs and an Ops contact (netops@helixmedtech.com). Ideally we'd like to avoid a long maintenance window for firewall changes during the pilot.

Can you confirm the minimal set of rules we should put in our allowlist for the private endpoint?

Thanks,
Noah
SRE, Helix MedTech

Attachment: network-diagrams.pdf (diagram stub)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Noah Patel <noah.patel@helixmedtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Gateway: IP binding & egress policy questions

Hi Noah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details below so your NetOps ticket can be concise: 

- Redwood can publish a curated, small set of stable egress IPs per deployment region for private endpoints. We recommend customers allowlist those for control-plane and model-serving egress.
- We publish those as a set of IP addresses (not a large CIDR). Rotations are rare and announced 30 days in advance; we also support a static NAT option for Dedicated/Private customers if you need zero change windows.
- Control plane endpoints use TLS 1.2+ with SNI. Mutual TLS is available for Private (on-prem/VPC) customers; it requires CSR/PKI exchange.
- Primary outbound port is 443. We do use outbound health-checks and metrics over TLS to specific endpoints; nothing in the ephemeral RTP range. Expect no additional TCP port openings.

Full details and a starter allowlist below: 

Recommended allowlist (minimal pilot):
- Control plane (TLS): 34.189.12.45, 34.189.12.46 (Redwood control-plane cluster, us-west-2)
- Model-serving egress (tokenized telemetry & cache invalidation): 52.204.78.120
- DNS: allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to your existing resolvers (Redwood will not force tunneled DNS)

Options if you prefer customer-managed egress:
- Customer NAT/proxy: Route all outbound traffic from the private endpoint through your NAT and allowlist the NAT IP(s) in our service config — we can accept that model and provide a minimal set of endpoints to test against.
- Static egress binding: For Private/Dedicated customers we can configure a dedicated NAT with static IPs (long-lived) in coordination with your procurement — used by many regulated orgs.

I'll loop in Laura with a suggested technical checklist that Ops can paste into the NetOps ticket. Ben — can you add the pilot commercial notes for dedicated NAT pricing if they ask?

-Rachel
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Hi Helix NetOps team,

Below is a minimal set of rules and evidence items for the pilot deployment. Paste these into your ticket and we'll confirm in the cutover call.

Minimal allowlist entries (pilot):
- TCP 443 to 34.189.12.45 (control plane) — TLS, SNI header redwood-control.redwood.ai
- TCP 443 to 34.189.12.46 (control plane) — TLS, SNI header redwood-control.redwood.ai
- TCP 443 to 52.204.78.120 (serving egress for telemetry/cache invalidation)
- DNS outbound to your resolvers (UDP/TCP 53) — resolution must succeed for service discovery

Notes/Constraints:
- If you deploy a customer NAT/proxy, allowlist the NAT IP(s) instead of Redwood IPs and provide those NAT IPs to us; we will route callbacks and telemetry to that NAT.
- For strict-zero-change windows: request dedicated static egress (procurement + Ops coordination). Pricing/contact: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.ai).
- Mutual TLS: available; requires CSR exchange and certificate enrollment (timeline: ~5 business days).

Evidence requested for SOC/Procurement signoff:
- Export of Redwood egress IP list (attached csv).
- TLS certificate chain and signature algorithm for control-plane endpoints (we will provide via secure share).
- Network diagram mapping (you provided; thanks).

Attachment: egress-ip-list-20270407.csv (stub)

Let us know an Ops contact for the cutover call and a preferred change window.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
